name: Scope
text: Analyze the video with Gemini 3.1 Ultra first—its multimodal strength means it can catch tone, emphasis, and visual cues the transcript misses. The trade-off is higher compute cost, but the payoff is richer context we’d otherwise miss. If that fails to surface key insights, fall back to manual review of timestamps flagged by the model.

name: Frame
text: The real risk isn’t compute cost—it’s that Gemini 3.1 Ultra’s multimodal output could mislead us by overinterpreting tone or visual cues we can’t verify. A better alternative is to first run the transcript through a lightweight sentiment analysis tool to flag sections needing deeper review, then use Gemini only on those segments. Settle it by testing both approaches on a 5-minute clip and comparing the quality of insights against the transcript alone.

name: Scope

Run the transcript through lightweight sentiment analysis first. It’s fast, cheap, and flags emotional spikes or contradictions the transcript alone misses—letting us target only the high-value moments for Gemini’s multimodal dive. The trade-off is missing subtle visual cues in the silent sections, but those rarely carry decisive context. This keeps compute costs low while ensuring we don’t waste time on unproductive analysis.

name: Iris
text:
